For that topic, validateEvent requires a string id, version 1, an allowed place id (oslo, helsinki, lisbon), string name, finite coordinates, type forecast.updated, valid updatedAt/fetchedAt timestamps, fixture or live mode, and 1–6 periods. Each period needs a valid time, finite temperature, null or finite nonnegative precipitation, and a string symbol. Parse or validation failures, including UNKNOWN_TOPIC, are caught, recorded as INVALID_EVENT, and followed by offset plus one; reject-write or offset-commit errors propagate. On valid input, applyEvent inserts the id into inbox in a transaction. A duplicate commits and returns DUPLICATE without changing the card. A new forecast can insert its card directly from event.place, without a prior place-requested event; an existing card updates only when its stored timestamp is null or older, while equal or older timestamps leave it unchanged and return OLDER_OR_EQUAL. Connected-client transaction errors attempt rollback and release in finally; connection errors occur before the try, and either failure prevents the offset commit. The DB transaction commits before the offset, so a later offset failure can replay the message; inbox suppresses a second card update, not duplicate delivery. Runtime remains unverified.

fragment.text: pool.connect runs before applyEvent's try. If it fails, there is no transaction rollback or client release. Once connected, errors inside the try attempt ROLLBACK, rethrow, and release the client in finally; either error prevents consumeMessage from reaching its valid-path offset commit. The DB transaction commits before the offset commit, so an offset failure can replay the message; the inbox duplicate check prevents a second card update, but does not establish exactly-once delivery.
